channel.title: Muhammad Hassan Raza
channel.description: Muhammad Hassan Raza runs product and engineering at Entropy Labs, builds backend and AI systems that hold up in production, and gets patches merged into open-source tools like kitty, calibre and libtorrent.

item.title: kitty's Parallel Test Runner Said OK While Its Workers Crashed
item.description: A missing addSubTest and an ignored exit status let kitty's new parallel test runner report success after failures. Fixing that exposed seven segfaulting workers on my Mac, and Kovid Goyal fixed those his own way.

item.title: Taking Obelisk's Backend Deploy From 54 Minutes to 32
item.description: Our backend deploys had crept up to almost an hour. Docker was fine. Most of the time went to migration tests waiting on one Postgres advisory lock, and to five Cloud Run services promoted one at a time.

item.title: PgBouncer Transaction Pooling Broke Row-Level Security in Polaris
item.description: I put PgBouncer in front of Postgres to stop a login outage. Two weeks later customer search started returning empty lists on some requests, because tenant isolation depended on a session variable and transaction pooling doesn't keep sessions.

item.title: Moving SMS Realtime Off Postgres Polling and Onto Redis Streams
item.description: A Django app whose SSE endpoints polled Postgres from sleeping request threads, and the outbox, relay and Redis Streams setup that replaced them in March 2026.

item.title: Cogitator
item.description: A local code search engine in about 500 lines of OCaml: TF-IDF over code chunks, ranked by cosine similarity, printed as context for an LLM.

item.title: October
item.description: A campaign platform where brands, agencies and creators run influencer campaigns from brief to report, with numbers every side can trust.

item.title: RISQ
item.description: Scoring intake calls for mass tort firms: separating real claimants from coached callers, with evidence a reviewer can follow.

item.title: The Best Way to Learn a Codebase Is to Break Someone Else's
item.description: What maintainers of kitty, calibre, libtorrent and Fallow taught me in review threads, usually by explaining why my fix was wrong in a way I hadn't considered.

item.title: Every Abstraction I Regret
item.description: A short list of abstractions I added too early, why they got worse over time, and the heuristics I use now to avoid repeating it.

item.title: How Fallow Analyzes TypeScript in Under a Second
item.description: How Fallow gets dead-code and dependency analysis done fast by skipping the TypeScript compiler, flattening graph storage, and doing the work in Rust.

item.title: Scoring Fraud in Legal Intake Calls
item.description: Coached callers, invented doctors and borrowed photos. How RISQ scores intake calls for mass tort firms, and why the most useful score is the one that grades the interviewer.

item.title: How Pyscn Analyzes Python with Go and tree-sitter
item.description: How Pyscn uses Go and tree-sitter to analyze Python code quickly for dead code, clone detection, and dependency insight.

item.title: Agent Middleware: What Kept Obelisk's Agents in Line
item.description: Obelisk runs more than fifteen specialist agents. Model choice, context, cost, retries and approvals all ended up in a middleware layer around them, and this is how that layer works.

item.title: LLMs Can't Save Bad UX
item.description: When an AI feature flops, look at the UX before you blame the model. Three features I watched fail, what fixed them, and the questions I now ask before anyone writes a prompt.

item.title: Most of My Pull Requests Started as an Annoyance
item.description: Drive-by fixes in qBittorrent, Dokploy and django-hijack: which ones merged, which didn't, and what the rejections taught me about scope.

item.title: Structured Logging for AI Debugging
item.description: Logging one structured event per request with evlog, so an AI assistant can follow what happened in a request.

item.title: TF-IDF in OCaml: When Functional Programming Clicks
item.description: Building a local code search engine in OCaml was a good excuse to learn TF-IDF, pure pipelines, and where immutability helps.

item.title: I Shipped a Race Condition That Oversold Stock (And Other War Stories)
item.description: Two cashiers selling the last item, a chain that returned nothing, and a lock that only worked when both requests hit the same process. Bugs I shipped, and the small fixes that held.

item.title: Anatomia
item.description: A nurse callback and case review product where transcripts, AI triage and follow-up calls all have to stay attached to the right patient.

item.title: Bonnet
item.description: An AI brand-development tool that turns a creative brief into research, strategy, creative direction, moodboards and a document a team can use.

item.title: Go Load Balancer
item.description: A small HTTP load balancer and dashboard in Go, built to understand what a reverse proxy actually does before trusting one.

item.title: LangChain in Production: What the Tutorials Leave Out
item.description: Where LangChain is worth using, where it gets in the way, and the defaults that stop our AI features failing silently: timeouts, validation, persistent state, tracing and pinned versions.

item.title: Obelisk
item.description: An AI marketing platform where specialist agents write, plan and analyze from a company's own material, without leaking one customer's brand into another's.

item.title: Free Web Dev Platforms Worth Your Time
item.description: A practical shortlist of free web development learning platforms and how to use them without getting stuck in tutorials.

item.title: Final Year Project (FYP) Guide for Students
item.description: A practical final year project guide for choosing scope, building steadily, avoiding weak ideas, and presenting work clearly.

item.title: Smart Dustbin: IoT with Arduino, Python, Kotlin & Azure
item.description: An IoT garbage monitoring system built with Arduino sensors, ESP8266 WiFi, a Python desktop dashboard, and a Kotlin Android app, plus what it taught me about hardware constraints.

item.title: Building a C++ Image Editor
item.description: My university project, a grayscale image editor in C++ that loads, filters and transforms PGM images.

item.title: PixelCryptor: Hiding Executables Inside Images
item.description: A Django project that embeds executable files within images using delimiter-based concatenation, and why real steganography is harder than this.

item.title: Fiction Books
item.description: Fantasy, science fiction and a few classics I keep pressing on people.

item.title: Non-Fiction Books
item.description: Geopolitics, psychology, and a couple of books about why people do what they do.
